exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-471 requires modification of data assumed to be immutable. The code uses file modification times for decisions, but there's no evidence these times are assumed immutable or that they're being modified.

connection.evidence: User-controlled 'newer' option and file system metadata (st.mtime) connect to the extraction decision. When enabled, newer files are skipped, but attacker control over file timestamps is speculative.

diff_causality.evidence: The added line implements the skip-newer functionality. Reverting would remove the bypass mechanism and force file updates regardless of modification times.

security_control.required_control: Protection against modification of assumed-immutable file metadata
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-471 requires protecting data assumed to be immutable from modification
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No evidence that file modification times are assumed immutable or that protection against their modification is required for this functionality

concrete_impact.evidence: Potential impact on file integrity if outdated files are preserved, but no demonstrated security consequence. The behavior may be intentional for performance or user preference.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, files would always be extracted regardless of modification times, eliminating the skip-newer bypass mechanism entirely.
supporting_evidence: Line 208 implements conditional file extraction bypass based on modification time comparison
The 'newer' option enables this time-based skipping behavior
contradicting_evidence: File modification times are not assumed immutable in the code - they're explicitly checked and compared
The behavior appears to be intentional functionality rather than a vulnerability
No evidence that file timestamps are treated as security-critical immutable data
unresolved_facts: Whether file modification times are security-critical immutable data in this context
Attacker ability to manipulate file timestamps to exploit this behavior
Whether skipping newer files is an intentional security feature or unintended bypass
